summary: 1922 plan for a 60-foot timber lookout on Fly Peak, Cochise County, AZ, at 9,790 ft; now listed as gone, and no source read describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; no source read says what remains or when it came down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1922 item says Mount Fly in the Chiracahua forest, Forest Lookouts says Fly Peak in Cochise County, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list says Flys Peak in Cochise County. The story treats them as one site, matched on name and county. The coordinates in the brief come from the Forest Fire Lookout Association list; the Forest Lookouts page gives no coordinates, so the match rests on name and county.

notes_for_editor: Only one 1922 newspaper item (reprinted) and one 'Tower Gone' listing were readable. Other pages could not be read: mindat.org (HTTP 403) describes Fly Peak as a former Forest Service fire tower location; the surgent.net Chiricahua Crest page failed with an SSL certificate error; landarts.org (HTTP 403) is unverified. A search snippet from surgent.net mentions a 'foundation of the lookout' at Flys Peak. That is unverified and not used in the story; if the page can be read, it may add a present-day site description. Completion date, staffing, fires and removal are not in any readable source. Access is unknown, so no access fact is recorded.
